object_description: two differentiated volumes linked by bayonet-shaped common spaces
design_condition: The project organizes the site through two main paths and a courtyard expansion, while the relocated sports fields and teacher parking access disrupt the intended linear park and transversal connections.

positive.statement: The meeting of the two orientation-cycle poles and their clear distinction from the sports pole were appreciated.

position.rationale: Distinct linear volumes and their separation are clearly visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The bayonet-shaped common spaces offer two inverse perceptions toward different horizons.

position.rationale: The central zigzag connection is directly legible between the two larger volumes.

positive.statement: The courtyard clearly delimits recreation spaces, whose shape is refined by the staggered positioning of the buildings.

position.rationale: The open court is visible between staggered building edges at ground level.

positive.statement: The project recognizes the structuring nature of the linear park through two main paths.

position.target: linear park and two main paths
position.rationale: The elongated two-part arrangement provides a plausible linear park anchor.

negative.statement: The relationship between common spaces and classes is too simple, weakening possibilities for use and appropriation.

position.rationale: A central internal zone approximates the relationship between shared and teaching spaces.

negative.statement: The systematic width of the premises produces configurations that are difficult to reconcile with teaching spaces.

position.rationale: A representative room zone anchors the criticized systematic width.

negative.statement: Moving the sports fields onto the central lawn contradicts the linear system and hinders transversal uses.

position.rationale: The central low site area represents the landscape interruption by sports uses.

negative.statement: The teacher parking access interrupts the connection to the green area.

position.rationale: A peripheral ground anchor approximates the access interruption to the green area.

negative.statement: The large pool reads more as an urban square and seems inadequate because students could divert its intended use.

position.rationale: The detached rectangular ground-level element is the strongest pool-like sampled feature.

negative.statement: Supplying the pool through rainwater harvesting seems implausible.

position.rationale: Water-supply plausibility is operational and lacks a visible geometric marker.

negative.statement: The remaining park design lacks sufficient substance to characterize the place within the sequence of green spaces.

position.rationale: A broad peripheral ground region represents the insufficiently characterized park.
